prompt: What are the best Heroku alternatives in 2026?

result.text:
Best Heroku Alternatives in 2026

If you're looking to move away from Heroku in 2026, there are several excellent alternatives offering simpler deployments, better pricing, modern developer workflows, and more infrastructure flexibility.

The best choice depends on what you're hosting: Node.js applications, Python/Django APIs, Ruby on Rails, Docker containers, background workers, or full-stack applications.

Here are my top recommendations.

1. Top 7 Heroku alternatives

1. Render — Best overall alternative

Render

Render is probably the closest replacement for Heroku.

It offers a similar deployment experience without requiring you to manage servers.

Key features:

GitHub and GitLab integration.
Automatic deployments.
Node.js, Python, Ruby, Go, and Docker support.
Managed PostgreSQL databases.
Background workers and cron jobs.
Preview environments.
Persistent disks.

Pricing: Free tier available; paid web services start around $7/month.

Best for: Developers migrating existing Heroku applications who want minimal changes to their deployment workflow.

2. Railway — Best developer experience

Railway

Railway is one of the most developer-friendly deployment platforms available.

Its visual interface makes it easy to deploy applications, databases, and supporting services.

Key features:

GitHub-based deployments.
Automatic builds and deployments.
Docker support.
PostgreSQL, Redis, and MySQL.
Environment variables and secrets.
Background workers.
Usage-based billing.
Easy service-to-service networking.

Pricing: Hobby plan starts at $5/month, including $5 in usage.

Best for: Startups, indie developers, APIs, and applications requiring multiple interconnected services.

3. Fly.io — Best for global applications

Fly.io

Fly.io is particularly interesting if you need more control over where your applications run.

Unlike traditional PaaS platforms, Fly.io runs applications as lightweight virtual machines across multiple geographic regions.

Key features:

Global application deployment.
Docker-based deployments.
Custom VM configurations.
Persistent storage.
Private networking.
Flexible scaling.
Support for background processes.

Pricing: Usage-based, with small instances costing a few dollars monthly.

Best for: Distributed applications, APIs, real-time services, and applications requiring low latency across different regions.

4. DigitalOcean App Platform — Best for predictable pricing

DigitalOcean App Platform

DigitalOcean App Platform provides managed application hosting without requiring you to manage servers.

It's particularly attractive if you already use DigitalOcean infrastructure.

Key features:

GitHub and GitLab deployments.
Managed databases.
Automatic deployments.
Autoscaling.
Docker support.
Static websites and backend applications.
Integrated cloud infrastructure.

Pricing: Starts around $5/month for basic application instances.

Best for: Small businesses, SaaS applications, and teams looking for straightforward infrastructure pricing.

5. Northflank — Best for advanced deployments

Northflank

Northflank offers a powerful platform for deploying applications, databases, and microservices.

It provides more infrastructure flexibility than traditional Heroku-style platforms.

Key features:

Docker and Kubernetes support.
CI/CD pipelines.
Managed databases.
Background jobs.
Preview environments.
Autoscaling.
Deployment across cloud infrastructure.

Best for: Growing SaaS companies, engineering teams, and microservices architectures.

6. Coolify — Best open-source alternative

Coolify

Coolify is an open-source, self-hostable alternative to Heroku.

It allows you to deploy applications on your own VPS instead of paying a managed hosting provider.

Key features:

Git-based deployments.
Docker support.
PostgreSQL, MySQL, and Redis.
Automatic SSL certificates.
Environment variable management.
Background workers.
Multiple server management.
No platform-specific application hosting fees.

Pricing: Free and open-source software; you pay for your server infrastructure.

Best for: Developers who want infrastructure ownership, lower hosting costs, and less vendor lock-in.

7. Vercel — Best for frontend applications

Vercel

Vercel is an excellent choice if your Heroku application is primarily a frontend application or uses Next.js.

Key features:

Excellent Next.js integration.
Git-based deployments.
Automatic preview deployments.
Serverless functions.
Edge functions.
Global CDN.
Built-in analytics.

Pricing: Free Hobby plan; Pro starts at $20/month.

Best for: Next.js, React, frontend applications, and serverless applications.

One limitation: Vercel isn't a direct replacement for Heroku when you need persistent background workers or long-running backend processes.

4. What happened to Heroku in 2026?

One important reason developers are exploring alternatives is that Heroku announced a transition to a sustaining engineering model in February 2026.

This means:

Heroku is prioritizing stability, security, and reliability.
New feature development is no longer its focus.
New Enterprise Account contracts are no longer being offered.
Existing customers can continue using the platform.

Heroku hasn't announced that it is shutting down. However, developers starting new projects may prefer platforms with more active product development.

5. My final recommendation

If I were choosing a Heroku replacement in November 2026, my shortlist would be:

Render: Best direct replacement. I'd start here for existing Heroku applications.
Railway: Best overall developer experience. Particularly good for startups and new projects.
Coolify: Best if hosting costs and infrastructure ownership are priorities.
Fly.io: Best for applications requiring global deployment.
DigitalOcean: Best if you want managed infrastructure with a broader cloud ecosystem.

My overall winner: Render.

It offers the closest experience to Heroku while supporting the major components developers typically need: application hosting, databases, background workers, cron jobs, and automated deployments.

For a new SaaS project, however, I'd seriously consider Railway as well.

One important question: Are you looking for a Heroku replacement for an existing application (Node.js, Python, Django, Rails, etc.), or are you choosing a platform for a completely new project?

That distinction can significantly change which platform I'd recommend.
